about: Surprised Koala is a photo of a grey koala clinging to a tree trunk, a big eucalyptus leaf sticking out of its mouth mid-chew, staring straight at the camera with round brown eyes. It looks like someone who was caught eating at the wrong moment and froze. The meme uses that stunned, mouth-full stare for being caught off guard, for genuine surprise when something unexpectedly works, or for fake shock at an outcome everyone saw coming. The leaf adds a guilty, caught-in-the-act feel that a plain shocked face wouldn't have.
usage:
Use the top box to set up the situation and the bottom box for the surprising twist, often split from one sentence: "when the code" / "works first try". You can also use the bottom box alone for the caught-in-the-act reading: "me when mom walks in at 3am".

It works best with mild, low-stakes surprises rather than tragedy: a reply arriving instantly, a teacher remembering your name, the bus actually being on time, your team winning a match you'd written off. The koala's frozen chewing pose also makes a great reaction to being called on unexpectedly.
